subject.title: PR5/5 durable core: internal session delivery handoff

question: Should OpenClaw adopt this cumulative durable-runtime architecture on the 2026.7.1 release line, with `delivered` defined as persisted internal session-queue ownership rather than external or user-visible delivery?
rationale: The PR establishes new cross-cutting persistence, protocol, recovery, and operator contracts; automated review cannot determine whether that architecture and release sequencing match maintainer intent.

options.title: Sponsor after gates
options.body: Approve the architecture in principle, then require immutable tooling, predecessor sequencing, upgrade proof, and exact-head restart evidence before merge.

options.title: Narrow to existing recovery
options.body: Keep the existing restart-sentinel and session-delivery architecture and extract bounded fixes that do not introduce the durable-runtime substrate.

options.title: Pause the release stack
options.body: Defer the release-line stack until a separately approved durable-runtime design and migration plan exists.

recommendation.title: Sponsor after gates
recommendation.body: Approve the architecture in principle, then require immutable tooling, predecessor sequencing, upgrade proof, and exact-head restart evidence before merge.

likelyOwner.reason: This person has the strongest recent restart-handoff history and was explicitly pulled into the current PR discussion.
